skills.name: create_shift
skills.description: Skill for creating ONE single shift/order (Bestellung) in the system. Every order MUST be billed to a customer, so a valid clientId of a customer (EntityTypeEnum.Customer) is required. A multi-part 24h service is modelled as ONE order with the full span (e.g. 07:00-07:00) and is afterwards cut into parts via cut_shift — never by calling this skill several times.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the shift (e.g. 'Frühdienst Bern', 'Spätdienst', 'Nachtdienst')

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: UUID of the customer (EntityTypeEnum.Customer) the order is billed to. REQUIRED. Resolve it with find_customer_candidates, or create a new customer via create_employee using entityType=Customer.

parameters.name: macroId
parameters.description: Optional UUID of the calculation macro. Leave empty to apply the standard default (the 'Shift'-category macro). Only set it when the user explicitly names a different macro; use list_macros to resolve the id.

parameters.name: abbreviation
parameters.description: Short abbreviation (e.g. 'FD', 'SD', 'ND'). Auto-generated from name if not provided.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description: Start time in HH:mm format (e.g. '07:00', '15:00', '23:00')

parameters.name: endTime
parameters.description: End time in HH:mm format (e.g. '15:00', '23:00', '07:00'). Can be before startTime for overnight shifts.

parameters.name: fromDate
parameters.description: Start date of the order validity in YYYY-MM-DD format. REQUIRED — this is when the order becomes valid/plannable. Always ASK the user (ab wann gilt die Bestellung) and offer a date picker by appending [REPLIES:date "Ab wann gilt die Bestellung?"]; NEVER silently assume today. Only resolve casual phrases the user actually said (heute/sofort -> today, morgen -> tomorrow).

parameters.name: untilDate
parameters.description: Optional end date of the order validity in YYYY-MM-DD format. Leave empty for ongoing/unlimited orders. If the user wants an end date, offer a picker [REPLIES:date "Bis wann gilt die Bestellung?"]. Must be >= fromDate.

parameters.name: weekdays
parameters.description: Which days the shift is active. Use the keyword 'all' (every day), 'weekdays' (Mon-Fri) or 'weekend' (Sat-Sun); or a comma-separated list of canonical English day tokens: Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri,Sat,Sun. Map any language the user uses to these canonical tokens.

parameters.name: sumEmployees
parameters.description: Number of employees (staff count / MA-Zahl) needed per shift occurrence. At least 1.

parameters.name: quantity
parameters.description: Quantity (Menge) of the order. At least 1. Defaults to 1; only set it when the user asks for a specific quantity.

parameters.name: groupIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of group IDs (GUIDs) to assign the shift to. Use list_groups to find IDs.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Optional description of the shift

parameters.name: asDraft
parameters.description: Optional, defaults to false. When true, creates the order as an editable draft (status OriginalOrder) instead of sealing it immediately — no plannable shift is created yet and cut_shift cannot be used until seal_shift runs. Structural reuse-matching against existing sealed orders is skipped for drafts.

skills.name: find_customer_candidates
skills.description: Lists existing customers (clients of type Customer) so you can ASK the user which customer a new order is billed to, before creating it. Every order MUST be billed to a customer. Call this whenever a new order/Bestellung is requested and the customer is not known yet. If none fits, the user can create a new customer with create_employee using entityType=Customer. Do not create the order before the customer is chosen.

parameters.name: searchString
parameters.description: Optional text filter on company name, first name or last name.

skills.name: find_split_shift_candidates
skills.description: Lists existing orders (Bestellungen) and already-split shifts of a group so you can ASK the user, before building a multi-part service, whether to reuse an existing already-split order or open a NEW one. ALWAYS call this FIRST when the user asks for a split / 24h-rotation / early-late-night service. Returns each order with its time span and, if already split, its parts. Do not create or cut anything before the user has chosen.

parameters.name: groupName
parameters.description: Name of the group to inspect (e.g. 'Biel/Bienne'). Use list_groups to find group names.

parameters.name: searchString
parameters.description: Optional text filter on the order name.

skills.name: cut_shift
skills.description: Cuts ONE existing plannable shift (an OriginalShift, e.g. a 24h order 07:00-07:00) into several time parts (split shifts) that all stay linked to the same order — the correct way to model an early/late/night rotation. NEVER create several independent shifts for the parts of one service: create ONE order with create_shift, then cut it here.

parameters.name: shiftId
parameters.description: UUID of the plannable shift (OriginalShift) to cut — the ShiftId returned by create_shift, or an order id found via find_split_shift_candidates.

parameters.name: parts
parameters.description: Comma-separated time ranges 'HH:mm-HH:mm' that tile the order span, e.g. '07:00-15:00,15:00-23:00,23:00-07:00' for an early/late/night split. A part whose end is not after its start is treated as crossing midnight.

parameters.name: partNames
parameters.description: Optional comma-separated names for the parts, aligned by index (e.g. 'Frühdienst Biel,Spätdienst Biel,Nachtdienst Biel'). Auto-named from the order if omitted.
